GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: Why proportional sync is the right primitive. The two panes are different projections of one markdown string: muya renders blocks with wildly different heights than the source lines (a one-line image vs a hundred-line code fence), so no cheap bijection exists between their scroll offsets. Proportional mapping (scrollTop fraction x target scrollHeight) is what Typora-class split editors ship; it drifts on height-skewed documents but never lies about direction, costs one division per rAF, and degrades to "roughly the same region" instead of "wrong end of the document" (today's state).

Alternatives.Alternative: Line-exact sync via a block-to-source-line anchor map (muya blocks carry start positions; CodeMirror has lineHeight). Better fidelity on code-heavy documents, but the map breaks on every list renumber, front-matter shift and paste; rejected for v1 (NonGoal), revisit only if owners report the drift as pain.

One-way sync (editable pane drives, never back). Simpler and loop-free, but reading either pane is the owner's actual use case ("when viewing"), and with dual editing coming (C-SPLIT-DUAL-EDIT) both panes will be drivers; the guard is unavoidable, so bidirectional comes almost free.

Scroll-position sync through the tab store (reuse updateScrollPosition). Rejected: the store offset is a single integer per tab for restore-on-open; two panes need a live channel, and polluting the persisted field with split-time chatter risks regressing C-FILE-POSITION-MEMORY restore semantics.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Sync controller placement: splitView.vue-local composable vs a new util module with its own graph anchor. The plan decides after --parallel-preflight; the helpers are written pure either way so the choice cannot change behavior.

Whether divider drag re-anchors continuously or only on drag-end (R-1 says "keeps the anchor visible"; continuous is the recommendation, drag-end the fallback if reflow cost shows up on huge documents).

Scenarios.Scenario: Long document, caret in section 60 of 120, split toggled on: rich pane centers the caret block; source pane opens at the matching fraction (~0.5), not at 0; one reflow is expected, the anchor must survive it with no visible jump afterwards.

Reading without any caret (restored tab, never focused): anchor falls back to the saved cursor of C-FILE-POSITION-MEMORY, else the top visible block fraction; the two panes still land in the same region.
Wheel over the rich pane, then immediately over the source pane: mastership follows the pointer; the guard swallows the programmatic echo so no ping-pong is observable.
Locked tab + split (once C-SPLIT-DUAL-EDIT lands): both panes read-only, scroll sync still works — viewing a locked document is exactly the reading case the owner described.
Tab switch while split is on: the incoming tab's panes align to its saved position (C-FILE-POSITION-MEMORY restore), not to the outgoing tab's offsets.
